caption:
6 claims that sit on top of the $1,000 standard deduction. Save this for your 2026–27 return.

The new standard deduction covers work-related expenses like uniforms, laundry, working from home and work car costs. These are separate, and they don't reduce it:

1. Union fees and professional association memberships.
2. Donations of $2 or more to a registered charity (a DGR).
3. Your registered tax agent's fee.
4. Income protection insurance premiums you pay yourself.
5. Personal super contributions you claim as a deduction (conditions apply).
6. Investment and rental property deductions.

So someone with $400 of union fees and a $250 tax agent fee still gets the full $1,000 as well.

The catch: unlike the standard deduction, each of these needs a record.

Which of these do you already claim?

#taxdeductions #taxreturn #australiantax #paylesslegally #standarddeduction
figures_checked: Standard deduction up to $1,000 from 2026–27, automatic, residents with labour income, no records; actual work claims reduce it; $300 work-expense and $150 laundry no-receipt exceptions end 1 July 2026; union fees, donations, tax agent fees, income protection premiums, personal super contributions, investment/rental deductions claimable on top (ATO Standard deduction for work-related expenses, updated 2 Nov 2026, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Registered tax agent fee deductible as cost of managing tax affairs; donations of $2 or more to a DGR with no benefit in return (ATO Deductions for donations, investments and managing your tax affairs, checked 15 Nov 2026)
